look.why: A crisp deep-ocean blue that highlights the classic countershaded slate-grey back and bright white underbelly.

habitat.text: Temperate and subtropical coastal and offshore waters worldwide, especially off California, South Africa, and southern Australia.

diet.text: Fish and rays as juveniles; seals, sea lions, dolphins, and whale carrion as large adults.

facts.text: Electroreceptors in its snout (ampullae of Lorenzini) detect tiny electrical pulses from a prey's heartbeat.
Keeps its swimming muscles warmer than surrounding cold ocean water, enabling explosive breaches above the surface.
